sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A low perennial or subshrub, about 20–50 cm tall, native to northern and western Europe. Its finely divided leaves are often densely white-haired, giving the plant a silvery appearance; small yellowish or brownish flower heads form narrow panicles. It grows in drier parts of salt marshes and on coastal banks.

sections.title: Related wormwoods and uses
sections.text: Artemisia absinthium is another silvery wormwood but is generally taller and is not specifically tied to salt marshes. No food use is verified in the sources consulted.
